added_models.model: Human CETP loss-of-function genotypes (common variants, truncating variants)

efficacy.note: Meta-analysis of CETP genotypes: variants lowering CETP activity carry higher HDL-C and slightly lower coronary risk, a genetic proxy for inhibition.
efficacy.quote: Three CETP genotypes that are associated with moderate inhibition of CETP activity (and, therefore, modestly higher HDL-C levels) show weakly inverse associations with coronary risk.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Europe PMC, PMID 18560005). Human CETP deficiency was described earlier (late 1980s); 2008 is a proxy for first use as a model of inhibition.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: HDL-C change (per-allele genotype effect vs drug % change)
efficacy.note: Genotypes predicted higher HDL-C with CETP inhibition; evacetrapib raised HDL-C 54-129% and cut LDL-C in dyslipidaemic patients.
efficacy.quote: Compared with placebo or statin monotherapy, evacetrapib as monotherapy or in combination with statins increased HDL-C levels and decreased LDL-C levels.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both sides; Nomura 2017 (Circ Res) full text read via PMC5523940.
efficacy.reason: Lipid surrogate matched; CHD prediction not borne out
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: Nicholls does not cite the genetics. Status follows the lipid surrogate (efficacy rule), so same. The genetic model also predicted lower coronary risk; Nomura 2017 (https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCRESAHA.117.311145) states that comparison after the fact, asking why evacetrapib and two others failed on CHD outcomes despite truncating-variant carriers having OR 0.70; that miss is carried by outcome_tested negative (ACCELERATE, a high-risk vascular population) and not scored as a status, as for the mouse track. Genotype effect is per allele and far smaller than the drug's, so direction_only.

patient_trials.quote: Although the cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitor evacetrapib had favorable effects on established lipid biomarkers, treatment with evacetrapib did not result in a lower rate of cardiovascular events than placebo among patients with high-risk vascular disease.

added_models.model: Animal allometric PK/PD model (hamster, rat, monkey PK + in-vitro potency), rocacetrapib

dose.note: Hamster, rat and monkey PK scaled allometrically and linked to an anacetrapib-anchored Emax model predicted a 25 mg daily efficacious human dose.
dose.quote: The predicted PK/PD profile and parameters were used to simulate the human PK/PD profiles for different dose levels, and based on the simulation result, the appropriate efficacious dose was estimated as 25 mg in a 60 kg human.
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC6680430). Year 2014 is a proxy: the first-in-human study NCT02156544 started 2014-06 at 25 mg, the predicted dose; the model's own date is not stated.

dose.magnitude_basis: absolute oral bioavailability (observed under one-fifth of predicted)
dose.note: Observed human bioavailability was under a fifth of the animal-scaled prediction, so predicted exposures and CETP inhibition were not reached at the predicted dose.
dose.quote: The prediction was unsuccessful, as a large discrepancy was highlighted from the observed profiles resulting from misprediction of the absolute bioavailability.
dose.confidence_note: Full text read; the authors give phase 1 data only as figures (FIH unpublished at submission). Human side is the single-ascending-dose study (Kim 2016, https://doi.org/10.2147/DDDT.S120387; NCT02156544, no results posted).
dose.judgement: Dose table row 'target never reached (PK)': at the model's 25 mg the exposure target was missed because absorption was overpredicted, so contra; efficacy for rocacetrapib stays untested (phase 2 NCT02977065 completed 2018 with no results posted). Kim 2020 (https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics12060573), a population model built on human data, recommended 200-400 mg for proof of concept, 8-16x the animal prediction. Not marked retrodiction: the model was built to choose the first-in-human dose and that study began at 25 mg, though its write-up followed the phase 1 data. Main-strip dose status (evacetrapib, same) is untouched; this is a separate track.

considered_not_added: Ference 2017 Mendelian randomization (CETP + HMGCR scores, apoB-proportional benefit): retrodiction of the class's outcome failures; the text available did not name a member drug, and the lipid comparison is already carried by the genetic track

Nomura 2017 CETP truncating variants: same system as cetp-lof-human-genetics; its stated CHD-outcome comparison with evacetrapib is recorded in that track's judgement, not as a status (efficacy follows the lipid surrogate)
Kim 2020 CKD-519 population PK/PD: built on human phase 1 data, not a preclinical model; used as patient-side context in the rocacetrapib dose entry
DRL-17822 population PK (Br J Clin Pharmacol 2020) and food-effect study: human-data models, no preclinical prediction compared
Lu 2015 lipoprotein kinetics model: run for RG7232, not a member drug
Gadkar 2016 HDL systems pharmacology model: no member-drug prediction compared with patient results
Cholesterol-fed rabbit / APOE*3Leiden.CETP mouse atherosclerosis: no study with a member drug found (rabbit work used torcetrapib/JTT-705, E3L.CETP used anacetrapib)
Patient-level systems (patient-derived cells, ex-vivo sensitivity, pharmacogenetics): none found for member drugs; ADCY9 pharmacogenetics concerns dalcetrapib, not a member
Rat BP / H295R and human CETP/apoA-I transgenic mouse: already tracked in the draft
